verses.text: So, holy brothers and sisters who share in the heavenly calling, focus on Jesus, the apostle and high priest we confess.
He was faithful to the one who appointed him, just as Moses was faithful in all God's household.
Jesus deserves greater glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house deserves more honor than the house itself.
Every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of everything.
Moses was faithful as a servant in all God's household, and his service pointed to what would be said later.
But Christ is faithful as the Son over God's household. We are his household if we hold firmly to our courage and the hope we celebrate, right to the end.
So, as the Holy Spirit says: ‘Today, if you hear his voice,
don't harden your hearts as in the rebellion, during the testing in the wilderness,
where your ancestors tested me and put me to the test, even though they saw what I did for forty years.
That's why I was angry with that generation and said, ‘Their hearts are always wandering; they haven't understood my ways.’
So I swore in my anger, ‘They will never enter my rest.’
Brothers and sisters, be careful that none of you has an evil, unbelieving heart that turns away from the living God.
Instead, encourage one another every day, while it's still called ‘today,’ so none of you will be hardened by sin's deception.
We share in Christ if we hold firmly to the confidence we had at the beginning, right to the end.
As Scripture says: ‘Today, if you hear his voice, don't harden your hearts as in the rebellion.’
Who were the ones who heard and rebelled? Weren't they all the people Moses led out of Egypt?
Who was God angry with for forty years? Wasn't it those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
And to whom did God swear they would never enter his rest? Wasn't it those who disobeyed?
So we see that they couldn't enter because they didn't believe.
